title: The jet that ran out of fuel because of one unit
summary: Air Canada Flight 143 was fuelled using pounds instead of kilograms, lost both engines over Manitoba, and glided to a safe landing at Gimli thanks to a glider-pilot captain.

title: The wall cleaner that became Play-Doh
summary: Play-Doh began in the 1930s as a wallpaper cleaner, nearly died when coal heating faded, and was saved when a teacher gave it to children.

title: The girl who fell three kilometres and walked out of the jungle
summary: In 1971 seventeen-year-old Juliane Koepcke fell about three kilometres from a broken airliner, then followed a stream for ten days to reach loggers, the only survivor of 92.

title: The bear who was an official soldier in World War Two
summary: Polish soldiers adopted a bear cub in Iran, then enlisted him with a rank so he could board a ship to Italy, where he carried ammunition crates at Monte Cassino.

title: The pope who put a dead pope on trial
summary: In 897 Pope Stephen VI had his dead predecessor Formosus dug up and tried in court; it ended with Stephen jailed and a ban on trials of the dead.

title: The ghost ship that drifted the Arctic for decades
summary: The cargo steamer Baychimo was abandoned in Alaskan ice in 1931, then kept being sighted drifting empty until 1969, and has never been found.

title: The Roman Empire that was sold at an auction
summary: In 193 AD the Praetorian Guard auctioned the Roman throne to Didius Julianus, who lasted only 66 days before Septimius Severus took Rome.

title: The Indian king who adopted hundreds of Polish children
summary: In 1942, Maharaja Digvijaysinhji of Nawanagar sheltered hundreds of Polish refugee children at Balachadi, and Warsaw later named a square after him.

title: The dropped socket that nearly set off America's biggest warhead
summary: In 1980 a repairman dropped a socket in an Arkansas Titan II silo; it punctured the fuel tank, the missile exploded, and its warhead landed nearby without detonating.

title: The dirty flask that gave us safety glass
summary: In 1903 chemist Édouard Benedictus knocked a flask off a shelf and it cracked without shattering, which led to laminated safety glass.

title: The steward who drifted alone for 133 days
summary: After a U-boat sank his ship in 1942, steward Poon Lim survived 133 days alone on a raft by making a fishhook, collecting rain and staying fit, until Brazilian fishermen found him.

title: The cavalry that captured a navy on horseback
summary: In January 1795 French hussars rode across frozen water and took the Dutch fleet at Den Helder, trapped in ice, without a naval battle.

title: The Indian man who was legally dead for nineteen years
summary: Lal Bihari of Uttar Pradesh was declared dead on paper in 1975 so relatives could take his land, and spent until 1994 proving he was alive.

title: The three lighthouse keepers who vanished from a rock in the sea
summary: In December 1900 all three keepers of the Flannan Isles lighthouse in Scotland disappeared, leaving an empty station and no answer.

title: The Roman emperor captured alive by Persia
summary: In 260 AD Persian king Shapur I captured Roman emperor Valerian, the only Roman emperor taken prisoner by an enemy, and Rome never got him back while its empire split apart.

title: The wall of thorns that crossed India
summary: The East India Company's Inland Customs Line, a thorny hedge guarded by thousands, stretched across India to enforce a salt tax, then was forgotten until Roy Moxham traced it in the 1990s.

title: The tiny relay setting that blacked out thirty million people
summary: On November 9, 1965, a protective relay near Niagara Falls set too low tripped and triggered a cascade that blacked out the Northeast US and Ontario.

title: The weed that stuck to a dog and became Velcro
summary: After a walk in the Alps in 1941, Swiss engineer George de Mestral studied the burrs stuck to his dog, copied their tiny hooks, and invented Velcro, which fashion laughed at before NASA used it.

title: The runner lost in the Sahara who survived on bats
summary: In 1994 Italian runner Mauro Prosperi was lost by a sandstorm during the Marathon des Sables, survived about nine days on bats from a shrine, and was found in Algeria far off course.

title: The pig that nearly started a war
summary: In 1859 an American farmer shot a British-owned pig on San Juan Island, triggering a standoff of warships and soldiers that lasted twelve years with no death except the pig.

title: The war Australia lost to birds
summary: In 1932 the Australian army sent machine guns against about twenty thousand emus ruining Western Australian wheat farms, and withdrew having failed to solve the problem.

title: The city that danced for weeks and nobody knows why
summary: In 1518 hundreds of people in Strasbourg danced for days without rest; the cause is still unknown.

title: The bronze jar that felt an earthquake nobody else could
summary: In 132 AD Han official Zhang Heng built a bronze seismoscope, and in 138 AD it sensed a distant earthquake that the capital never felt, proven when a messenger arrived days later.

title: The farmer who dug up the oldest zero in the world
summary: A farmer found the Bakhshali manuscript in 1881, and in 2017 radiocarbon dating showed its dot zero is centuries older than any zero known before.

title: The wave of beer that flooded a London street
summary: In 1814 a slipped iron hoop on a giant brewery vat let loose a flood of beer in London, killing eight, and a court called it an act of God.

title: The wrong part that became the pacemaker
summary: In 1956 engineer Wilson Greatbatch grabbed the wrong resistor, and his circuit pulsed like a heartbeat, leading to the implantable pacemaker.

title: The cook who survived sixty hours inside a sunken ship
summary: In 2013 Nigerian cook Harrison Okene survived about sixty hours in an air pocket inside a capsized tugboat on the seabed, until divers searching for bodies saw his hand move.

title: The bat bombs that burned down their own army base
summary: In World War Two the US tested bats carrying tiny timed fire devices, but escaped bats burned down part of an American army airfield and the project was cancelled.

title: The man who escaped slavery by mailing himself in a box
summary: In 1849 Henry Brown escaped slavery by being shipped 350 miles from Richmond to Philadelphia in a small wooden crate, and became known as Henry Box Brown.

title: The signal from space that was heard only once
summary: In 1977 Ohio's Big Ear telescope recorded a 72-second radio burst from Sagittarius that was never detected again, and its source is still unknown.
